newsitem.title: FRANCE: No cargo share on new JAL/Air France Nahoya route.
newsitem.headline: No cargo share on new JAL/Air France Nahoya route.

text.p: Japan Airlines and Air France's new twice, weekly code-share passenger flight between Paris and Nagoya will not entail co-operation on freight, a JAL cargo official told Reuters.

"We won't be reserving any cargo space at all on the Nagoya flight because frankly, we feel we are serving the city adequately at present via our six-times weekly passenger service to Osaka from Paris and of course our services to Tokyo. Nagoya will be a 100 percent Air France cargo destination," the official said.
An Air France Airbus 340-300 is to ply the route from July 1.
JAL has a block-space agreement with Air France on the French carrier's weekly 747F service between Paris and Osaka.
Air France and JAL jointly operate a four-times weekly Boeing 747F service between Paris and Tokyo.
Air France operates an additional freighter frequency independent of this agreement.

"No changes are planned in these freighter frequencies in the forseeable future. The market has picked up markedly since the beginning of March. However, at the moment, bookings can be made only one to two days in advance so there's no real squeeze on capacity unlike the equivalent period two years ago when customers had to wait one week to ten days to secure space," the official added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
